data.gender_notes: Barnaby is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Barnaby is derived from the Aramaic words bar (son) and nab (consolation). In the New Testament, Barnabas was an early Christian leader who encouraged and comforted Paul, taking him under his wing and promoting his teachings to the Christian community. The name Barnaby carries the meaning “Son of consolation” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Barnaby usually hope their child will grow to embody son of consolation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Barnaby belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of consolation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barnaby total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
